title: Deterministic calibration manifests and rollback playbook for quant artifacts
creator: Emily Chen
description: Problem: We need an unambiguous, reproducible way to identify and roll back quantization artifacts (FP8/INT8) produced by the calibration pipeline. Current artifacts can differ across runs due to RNG seeding, dataloader ordering, non-deterministic kernel behavior, and metadata drift (e.g., training env tags). That makes it hard to: reproduce regressions, validate accuracy across releases, and safely revert to a previously verified quantized model.
goal: Design and implement a deterministic calibration manifest format + checksum rules and an operational rollback playbook that allows: 1) exact reproduction of a calibration run; 2) content-addressable referencing of artifacts; 3) safe automated rollback during bad canary/rollout; 4) CI gating that detects non-semantic differences.
approach_summary: We will produce a canonical manifest for every quant artifact that includes: model base commit hash, model architecture fingerprint, calibration dataset fingerprint, ordered list of calibration slices (with checksums), fixed RNG seed(s), exact quantization config (profile + hyperparams), runtime kernel version, and build/container image digest. Each manifest is serialized using a stable protobuf schema and signed by the build system. The artifact storage will expose: artifact_sha256, manifest_sha256, and a derivation chain for dependent artifacts. The rollout tooling will use manifest matching and checksum comparisons to decide if an automated rollback is possible.
design_decisions:
1) Checksum algorithm: SHA-256 for artifact and manifest; BLAKE3 considered for speed but deferred due to ecosystem support.
2) Serialization: canonical protobuf v3 (field numbering and default handling enforced) to avoid whitespace/ordering diffs.
3) Calibration determinism: require explicit RNG seeds and deterministic dataloader ordering; we will add a test harness to CI that retries calibration with seeds fixed to assert bitwise-equality for artifacts.
4) Signed manifests: manifests will be signed with our infra keypair to prevent accidental tampering when storing in object storage.
5) Backcompat: store legacy metadata in a legacy_metadata field (string) but do not rely on it for hashing decisions.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Enforcing strict determinism increases engineering friction for third-party contributors (we will provide adapters).
- Canonical serialization makes minor metadata edits break checksums; mitigated by semantic diff tooling that understands the schema and can classify changes as benign vs. functional.
- Signing manifests requires key management; initial rollout will use an infra-managed key with rotation policy.
acceptance_criteria:
1) CI job reproduces a sample FP8 and INT8 calibration run twice with identical manifests and artifact_sha256.
2) Manifest schema reviewed and merged in internal RFC doc.
3) Canary rollout scenario: when a bad regression is detected by accuracy regression tests, the automated rollback uses manifest matching to revert to the previous artifact within the SLA window.
4) Release notes and runbook published in Confluence.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (2 sprints): define manifest schema, implement deterministic calibration harness, add canonical serializer in calibration library.
Phase 2 (2 sprints): artifact storage changes (store manifest + signatures), CI gating tests, and golden replays for FP8/INT8.
Phase 3 (1 sprint): rollout automation and rollback playbook in Console + runbook docs.

runbook_snippet: Rollback playbook (short): 1) detect regression via eval suite -> tag running rollout and capture active manifest_sha256; 2) query artifact store for previous stable manifest for same model base commit or matching model_arch_fingerprint; 3) verify candidate manifest signature and checksums; 4) trigger rollback via rollout service to replace model variant; 5) run quick smoke accuracy tests and notify on-call; 6) open postmortem if rollback triggered automatically.
postmortem_plan: If a rollback is triggered we will: capture the failing manifest and corresponding golden inputs, run a reproducibility job to assert whether calibration is deterministic given the manifest, and escalate to model-owner team if the failure is due to model architecture changes. Postmortem template lives in Confluence link above.
